subject: ACME MAP — Technical evaluation plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Grey <samantha.grey@acme.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MAP — Technical evaluation plan & success criteria

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great to meet today. Thanks for sharing more detail on ACME's real-time summarization use case and throughput expectations. Per our call, attached is a first draft of the Mutual Action Plan milestone that covers the Technical Evaluation Plan (MAP Milestone: Tech Eval). The draft includes proposed success criteria, latency/cost targets, model shortlist, responsibilities, and a suggested timeline.

Quick recap of the proposal highlights:
- Success criteria (minimum pass):
  - Quality: >= 90% pass rate on ACME-provided eval set (binary pass/fail rubric we discussed)
  - Latency: median request latency < 200ms; p95 < 400ms; p99 < 800ms for the 1–2k token response size distribution you described
  - Cost: target 1M tokens served for inference under $230 (hosted equivalent), with recommendations for dedicated quantized variants to drive below target if needed
- Model shortlist to benchmark: llama-3-70b-q4, mistral-instruct-7b, falcon-180b-instruct-8bit (our team will add one Redwood-verified variant as a control)
- Responsibilities:
  - ACME: provide representative eval dataset (anonymized), target request profile, and SLOs for user-facing latency; procurement contact to confirm contract timing
  - Redwood: run benchmarks, provide raw logs/latency histograms, cost estimates by model/quantization, and a short analysis doc with recommended production configuration
- Target milestone close date: 2026-08-31 (to align with your Q3 rollout window).

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached MAP draft and the benchmarking instructions (attached).
2) ACME to share the anonymized eval dataset and a sample traffic profile by Thu 23 Jul.
3) Procurement to confirm PO timeline and whether a short SOW is required before we begin benchmarking.
4) Redwood to provision a test pool once dataset is received (I’ve looped in Vivek to confirm infra).

I flagged a few open items in the PDF (page 2) — mostly around exact tokenization rules and whether you want hallucination thresholds tied to a strict rubric or a softer scoring approach.

If that timeline looks good, I’ll set a 30-minute kickoff for next Monday to align on dataset format and schedule.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: ACME_MAP_TechEval_Draft_v1.pdf, benchmarking-instructions.md

From: Samantha Grey <samantha.grey@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MAP — Technical evaluation plan & success criteria

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary and the draft looks like a solid starting point. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Eval dataset: we'll extract ~2k anonymized customer queries and provide expected outputs for ~300 of them as a labeled subset. We'll deliver in CSV with columns (query, expected_summary, token_budget). Is that format okay?
- Latency targets: the median <200ms is aggressive but aligns with our UX goal. Can you confirm whether the med/p95/p99 targets assume cold-starts excluded (i.e., warmed runtimes) and whether they include network hop to ACME infra?
- Cost estimate: the $230/1M tokens target is roughly in line with our budget — procurement cc'd to coordinate PO/contracting cadence.

Procurement note: we typically need a short SOW and 2–3 week PO window after SOW approval. We'll aim to get the SOW request in this week.

We'll plan to share the dataset by Thu 23 Jul and get back on the exact format if anything changes. Can we do the kickoff call Mon 27 Jul 09:00 PT?

—Samantha
Samantha Grey
Product Lead, Search & Summarization | ACME.ai
samantha.grey@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Grey <samantha.grey@acme.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MAP — Technical evaluation plan & success criteria

Samantha — thanks, that format works. Quick answers inline to your questions: 

- Dataset format: CSV with (query, expected_summary, token_budget) is perfect. If possible please include a small "category" column to help stratify results (e.g., 'long-form', 'bullet', 'legal').
- Latency assumptions: targets assume warmed runtimes (no cold-start bucket). Network hop: benchmarks will report both infra-to-infra compute latency and end-to-end latency including a single network hop (we'll label them clearly). We'll prioritize the end-to-end numbers for UX evaluation.
- Cost baseline: the draft cost target is a hosted-equivalent estimate. If you prefer Dedicated/quantized variants we can show delta estimates in the benchmarking report.

Timeline & kickoff: Monday 27 Jul 09:00 PT works for our team — I'll send calendar invite once procurement confirms SOW cadence.

Vivek — can you confirm we can provision a 8-GPU test pool (mixed A100/NVIDIA H100 equivalents) for the week after we receive the dataset? Also flag any model shortlist constraints (e.g., license or quantization availability).

Action items (summary):
- ACME: dataset + sample labels by Thu 23 Jul (Samantha)
- ACME procurement: indicate SOW/PO timing (procurement@acme.ai)
- Redwood: provision test pool upon dataset receipt (Vivek) and prepare benchmarking runner (Neha/Rishi)

Thanks —
Marissa

All — quick infra confirmation. We can provision an 8-GPU mixed test pool (A100-equivalent + H100-equivalent) starting Thu 23 Jul for an initial 2-week window. We'll tag the cluster for RDW-2026-0421 so Neha/Rishi can run the benchmarking harness.

Model shortlist notes: we'll include the three you called out plus a Redwood-verified control:
- llama-3-70b-q4 (quantized)
- mistral-instruct-7b
- falcon-180b-instruct-8bit
- redwood/benchmark-control-34b (control baseline)

Operational notes:
- We'll exclude cold-starts from the primary latency reported numbers; all runs will start with a warm-up phase.
- We'll provide median/p95/p99 histograms, token-level cost estimates, and the raw logs (anonymized) for auditability.
- ETA for first benchmark report (once dataset received): 10 business days. If ACME can provide the labeled subset earlier we can prioritize accuracy runs in parallel.

I'll set the cluster tagging and send a short infra runbook (attachment) to Neha/Rishi.

—Vivek
